Autonomous research agents are increasingly
used to automate large portions of scientific re-
search, yet they are prone to research integrity
violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise
the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of
the research process. We present RIDAR, a
framework for automated RIV detection and
runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT,
a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types
spanning the full research lifecycle. Build-
ing on RIVT, we present RIDAR-POST-HOC,
a framework to detect RIVs within agent tra-
jectories. RIDAR-POST-HOCachieves 85.2%
F1 performance on RIV-GOLD, a benchmark
for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated
trajectories. Applying RIDAR-POST-HOCto
RIV-WILD, a dataset of 300 agent trajecto-
ries across 50 distinct research tasks, we de-
tect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajec-
tories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in
current agents.

of RIVs in autonomous research agents,
we construct RIV-WILD, a dataset of 300 agent
trajectories collected from 6 frontier harness-model
configurations across 50 distinct research tasks.
RIDAR-POST-HOCidentifies 3,964 RIV instances
across 99.7% of these trajectories, with analysis re-
vealing how violation patterns vary across task and
RIV types. Finally, to test whether RIVs can be mit-
igated through runtime intervention, we construct
RIV-LIVE, a 60-trajectory subset of RIV-WILD
re-run with RIDAR-RUNTIMEintervention, each
paired with its non-intervened baseline. RIDAR-
RUNTIMEreduces the mean number of RIVs re-
maining at task completion from 14.9 to 9.4, yield-
ing a 36.8% decrease. These results show that
RIVs are widespread in current autonomous re-
search agents and that automated runtime interven-
tion offers an effective safeguard.

This work has several limitations. First, RIDAR
relies on LLM-based judgments. Although RI-
DAR achieves high agreement with human anno-
tations on RIV-GOLD, its performance may still
vary across backbone LLMs, research tasks, and
trajectory records. Human review therefore re-
mains necessary in high-stakes settings. Second,
the evaluation of RIDAR in this paper primarily
covers research tasks from domains of mathematics
and machine learning. We leave a broader evalua-
tion across other scientific domains to future work.
Finally, we study frontier general-purpose agent
harnesses because they are increasingly used by
researchers worldwide to assist and automate sci-
entific research, making their research integrity a
pressing concern. Our trajectories do not cover spe-
cialized research agent frameworks, and whether
the same patterns hold in such systems remains an
open question.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding detector precision/recall, the widespread nature of reporting violations in current autonomous agents, and the effectiveness of runtime interventions are well-aligned with tabular results, ablation experiments, and detailed error analyses [E3551b39bec139607-B0034, E3551b39bec139607-B0040, E3551b39bec139607-B0044].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated on RIV-GOLD (60 trajectories annotated by 17 human experts), achieving 85.2% instance-level F1 and 86.7% taxonomy F1 matched via an independent judge, evaluated on 300 diverse agent trajectories in RIV-WILD, and tested in a matched 60-trajectory live trial (RIV-LIVE) where runtime interventions reduced remaining violations by 36.8% [E3551b39bec139607-B0002, E3551b39bec139607-B0031, E3551b39bec139607-B0037, E3551b39bec139607-B0038, E3551b39bec139607-B0040].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: 17 independent human expert annotations on the RIV-GOLD dataset validate the detector's findings, showing 85.2% instance-level F1 and 87.1% precision [E3551b39bec139607-B0010, E3551b39bec139607-B0038, E3551b39bec139607-B0040].

is an iterative loop: each time the discovery is triggered,ExpEvolve fits a pairwise ranker on the
annotated idea factors, and selects the pairs of archived programs with a large score gap that the

programs to propose candidate idea factors that distinguish them. Each candidate is then annotated
on the whole archive, and is admitted into the idea memory if each of its values is supported by
enough programs and its values separate the scores.

Exploration at plateaus.Oftentimes, evolutionary discovery can concentrate around its best
programs and a single strategy. Consequently, the ideas widely used in top-scoring programs stop
varying, and their roles cannot be identified from the archive (Thm. 3.3). When the best score does
not improve for𝜅 generations, ExpEvolve switches to idea-guided exploration, which enforces the
mutator LLM to explore diverse ideas other than those widely used in top-scoring programs. Specifi-
cally, a separate LLM probes the properties shared by the top-scoring programs as background idea
factors, and an LLM judge determines which idea factors in the memory depend on the background.
ExpEvolve then masks the actions of the dependent idea factors, instructs the mutator LLM to avoid
them, and assigns more slots to random exploration with diversified demonstrations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains, sample efficiency improvements (up to several-fold fewer evaluations to match baseline scores), and the predictive accuracy of discovered factors over program orderings align well with the empirical data presented in the tables and figures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation benchmarks ExpEvolve against SCS and ShinkaEvolve across 11 established mathematical discovery tasks and integrates it into OpenRSI for 6 MLS-Bench tasks under matched evaluation budgets. Results report seed means, standard deviations, best seeds, and sample efficiency comparisons across multiple underlying LLMs.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the studied discovery domains remain restricted to relatively small-scale verification settings with automated/deterministic objective code, leaving expensive real-world verification regimes to future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formalizing evolutionary discovery as a POMDP and grounding the sample complexity gains of structured representations and exploration requirements in Theorems 3.1 and 3.3. evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported correlation between process-level No Error Rate and external benchmark accuracy provides a measurement independent of the GPT-5 judge, and its direction supports the diagnostic validity claim.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline findings are error distributions and process-reliability statistics produced by rule-based parsing plus GPT-5 LLM-as-a-judge classification, with terminal accuracy from external benchmark ground truths.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No agent or model is trained, tuned, selected, or otherwise adapted in this study; the work is a diagnostic benchmarking and error-analysis exercise over fixed agent frameworks and model backbones.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the prevalence and nature of intermediate execution errors are supported by quantitative step distributions, correlation with terminal accuracy, and qualitative case studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is tested on multiple datasets (BrowseComp, BrowseComp-zh, GAIA, XBench-DS, and DeepResearch Bench) comparing different model architectures. The empirical analysis demonstrates clear differentiations in failure profiles across models and shows a strong correlation between process-level reliability and terminal accuracy.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No optimization loop is performed; external benchmarks with ground-truth answers and standard evaluation criteria are used to measure final performance alongside error diagnosis.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Diagnostic classification of step traces using rule-based parsing and GPT-5 prompting alongside standard benchmark end-to-end task accuracy and report quality metrics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No models or agents were trained, tuned, or iteratively optimized against an internal metric in this benchmarking study.

primary.limitations: The work focuses on diagnostic categorization rather than online automated repair, evaluates a restricted toolset (search and fetch) in Deep Search, and relies partly on an LLM evaluator (GPT-5) for semantic task-level categorizations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology combines rule-based structural parsing with human-guided LLM-as-a-judge prompting to classify step-by-step agent execution traces into granular categories (such as tool mismatch, premature stopping, and synthesis hallucination). Evaluated traces are collected under controlled agent setups across multiple standard benchmarks.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides a clearly defined problem formulation, sound taxonomy, rigorous experimental trace diagnostics on established benchmarks, and actionable design insights for agent development, meeting the standards for scientific contribution.
primary.scoped_contribution: A diagnostic methodology and structured taxonomy categorizing intermediate execution errors of Deep Search and Deep Research LLM agents into system-level and task-level breakdowns across existing multi-step benchmarks.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides a clearly defined problem formulation, sound taxonomy, rigorous experimental trace diagnostics on established benchmarks, and actionable design insights for agent development, meeting the standards for scientific contribution.
